2609.20129.title: Local Sparsity Enables Unsupervised LLM Safety Detection
2609.20129.paper_summary: Deployment-time safety methods for large language models (LLMs) are predominantly supervised and assume access to unsafe training data. Nevertheless, new attacks and harm categories regularly arise, not captured by models trained in such a supervised fashion. An alternative approach is to view this problem through the lens of anomaly detection, namely, to rely solely on modeling safe data and flagging out-of-distribution inputs. However, LLM activations lie in a high-dimensional space, raising concerns about whether anomaly detection is statistically feasible. We show that, under the linear representation hypothesis (LRH), there may indeed be hope. In the LRH concept space, which is typically recovered via a sparse autoencoder (SAE), nearby points share a small common active support. Using this local sparsity insight, we propose a framework for locally masked SAE-based anomaly detection, supported by theoretical justifications. We validate it on various architectures and datasets, including both capability-testing datasets and safety-specific datasets. Finally, when we allow algorithms to use 1% out-of-distribution data for calibration, locally sparse methods achieve near-optimal performance, demonstrating their ability to capture meaningful safety information while using only 1-2% of SAE neurons for computation.
2609.20129.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）的部署時安全方法主要是監督式的，並假設可以訪問不安全的訓練數據。<lb/>然而，新的攻擊和危害類別經常出現，這些類別並未被以這種監督方式訓練的模型捕捉到。<lb/>一種替代方法是通過異常檢測的視角來看待這個問題，即僅依賴建模安全數據並標記分佈外的輸入。<lb/>然而，LLM 的激活位於高維空間中，這引發了對異常檢測在統計上是否可行的擔憂。<lb/>我們表明，在線性表示假設（LRH）下，確實可能存在希望。<lb/>在 LRH 概念空間中，通常通過稀疏自編碼器（SAE）恢復，附近的點共享一小部分共同的活動支持。<lb/>利用這一局部稀疏性洞察，我們提出了一個基於 SAE 的局部遮蔽異常檢測框架，並得到理論上的支持。<lb/>我們在各種架構和數據集上進行了驗證，包括能力測試數據集和安全特定數據集。<lb/>最後，當我們允許算法使用 1% 的分佈外數據進行校準時，局部稀疏方法達到了接近最佳的性能，證明了它們在僅使用 1-2% 的 SAE 神經元進行計算的同時捕捉有意義的安全信息的能力。
